prompt: You leave a $15\%$ tip on a \$$40$ meal. How much is the tip?
hint: Fifteen percent can be built from two easier percents, $10\%$ and $5\%$. Notice that $5\%$ is half of $10\%$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try the same problem with friendlier numbers first — say "20% of 50" — then come back to this one.
Fifteen percent can be built from two easier percents, $10\%$ and $5\%$. Notice that $5\%$ is half of $10\%$.
$10\%$ of $40$ is $4$ dollars, and $5\%$ is half of that, $2$ dollars. Add the two pieces to get $15\%$.

explanation: Split $15\%$ into $10\% + 5\%$, because each piece is easy to find mentally.
$10\%$ of $40$ is $40 \div 10 = 4$, and $5\%$ is half of that, which is $2$.
Add the pieces: $4 + 2 = 6$. The decimal method agrees, since $0.15 \times 40 = 6$.
The tip on the meal is $6$ dollars.
